key_insight: lPINN pretrains a nonlinear neural basis offline and solves new PDE or inverse problems online with only a final linear fit, combining reduced-order efficiency with physics-informed accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This makes physics-informed modeling much faster at deployment while retaining differentiability and compatibility with forward, inverse, and cross-resolution scientific computing tasks.
method: Learn continuous neural basis functions from an ensemble of solution data offline.
Pretrain the hidden layers using derivatives or physics residuals so the basis is operator-compatible.
Freeze the basis for each new case and optimize only the linear output layer using governing-equation, boundary, initial, and observation terms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports tests on advection-diffusion, Burgers', and nonlinear pendulum problems, with lower errors than vanilla PINNs and online speedups from about 10x to over 100x, especially when residual or measurement data are scarce.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and representativeness of the offline training ensemble, so basis transfer may degrade if new problems differ substantially from the pretrained regime.
paper_title: Linearized PINN with pretrained nonlinear layers
